subject: Competitive bake-off recap: NovaHealth - Redwood vs OmniServe
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@novahealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: NovaHealth - Redwood vs OmniServe

Hi Samira / Tom -

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

High-level pain points you shared:
- 95th percentile latency spikes during peak ingestion windows (affects clinician workflows)
- Cost per inference at scale (current provider costs are drifting above thresholds)
- Occasional hallucinations when summarizing long patient histories; need deterministic structured outputs for downstream apps
- Data residency / audit requirements for PHI (must be able to pin region and provide audit logs)
- Integration effort into your HL7/FHIR pipeline and model validation process

Goals you called out:
- Reduce inference unit cost by ~30% vs current baseline
- 95th percentile latency under 120ms for typical note summarization workstreams
- Clear SOC2 evidence and audit logs for security/compliance
- Minimal integration effort (SDKs + simple routing) and predictable rollout plan

Where Redwood sits in the bake-off (summary):
- Strengths: high-throughput runtime, intelligent batching/caching to reduce token cost, unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, strong observability for latency/cost per route
- Risks/Open items: we need to run your latency/load profile to validate 95th percentile under your real workload; also want to run a hallucination/regression eval on your sample data set

Decision criteria we captured (please confirm weights if you have them):
1) Latency under load
2) Unit cost at scale
3) Security/compliance evidence (SOC2, KMS integrations, audit logs)
4) Integration effort + SDK support
5) Post-deployment support / SLAs

Open questions / follow-ups from Redwood:
- Can you share a small (de-identified) sample of the workload we should use for the hallucination/regression tests?
- Are there preferred windows for a 2-hour load test next week?
- Do you have a scoring matrix or weightings for the bake-off we should align to?

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Redwood: will share a bake-off scorecard and two attachments (bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx, redwood-runtimesheet.pdf) with our baseline metrics and proposed test plan - Aditya (owner)
- Redwood Engineering: run the load test and hallucination eval on NovaHealth sample data - Rishi (owner)
- NovaHealth: confirm test windows and share de-identified sample dataset + scoring weights - Samira (owner)

Proposed test windows: Mon 8/24 or Tue 8/25 (we can do both to compare). Advise which works best for you.

Thanks - happy to sync for 15 minutes to confirm scope once you share the sample.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (555) 212-3344
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (scorecard template), redwood-runtimesheet.pdf (baseline perf summary)

From: Samira Khan <skhan@novahealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: NovaHealth - Redwood vs OmniServe

Aditya - thanks for the thorough recap. That aligns with our notes. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Scoring/weights: our procurement committee typically weights: latency (35%), cost (25%), security/compliance (20%), integration effort (10%), support/SLA (10%). If you can pre-fill the scorecard with Redwood's self-scores against those weights that would save time.

2) Timeline: we're aiming to select a vendor by end of September and go into pilots in October. So quick turnaround on tests would be appreciated.

3) Tests/data: we'll share a de-identified sample (FHIR snippets + clinical notes) by EOD Monday (8/17). For the latency/load test: the important KPI is 95th percentile under realistic concurrent load - our current spike is 4k qps aggregated; we don't expect you to match that in the POC but please run at 500-1,000 concurrent requests for an initial comparison.

4) Compliance: please provide SOC2 report (redacted if necessary) and a brief note on data residency options (hosting regions, logging/audit capabilities).

5) Integration: is your SDK compatible with our FHIR pipeline or do we need a custom adapter?

If you can get the scorecard and SOC2 evidence to us by Tue 8/18, we can prioritize scheduling the load test the week of 8/24.

Thanks - looking forward to the attachments.

Regards,
Samira Khan
Director, AI & Clinical Informatics | NovaHealth
skhan@novahealth.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Samira - thanks, that timeline and scoring weights make sense. Attached is the scorecard pre-filled with Redwood's self-assessment and the redwood-runtimesheet.pdf with baseline numbers we referenced. See a few quick answers below: 

- SOC2: we can provide the SOC2 Type II report under an NDA; alternatively we can provide a redacted copy for review. We support KMS integrations and provide audit logs per-request for dedicated/private deployments.
- SDK/FHIR: our SDK is language-agnostic and we have a reference adapter for FHIR ingestors used by two health customers; in many cases customers use the SDK to wrap a small adapter. We'll share the adapter docs.
- Load test: we propose Tue 8/24 09:00-11:00 PT as primary window and Wed 8/25 09:00-11:00 PT as a fallback. Rishi will run the tests and capture 50/90/95/99th percentile latencies and error rates.

Action items (updated):

- Samira: share de-identified dataset + confirm which of the proposed windows works

If that all sounds good I'll lock the Tue window - Rishi, can you confirm?

Hi Samira / Tom -

Confirming Redwood will run the load and regression tests on Tue 8/24 09:00-11:00 PT. Plan below: 

Test plan (summary):
- Load profile: 500 concurrent clients for 60 minutes, then 1,000 concurrent clients in 10-minute bursts to emulate spikes
- Workload mix: 60% short chat-style generation (tokens ~30-80), 40% long note summarization (tokens ~800-2,000) using your de-identified samples
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tail latency distribution, error rate, token throughput, cost estimate per 1M tokens
- Hallucination/regression: run our hallucination eval harness on your supplied samples (F1/precision/recall for structured extraction tasks + qualitative false-positive log)
- Report deliverable: CSV with raw metrics + PDF summary and a filled scorecard with pass/fail flags and suggested mitigations

Pre-test checklist:
- Samira: please upload de-identified samples to the Drive folder (shared link below) and confirm any rate limits or downstream constraints
- Aditya: confirm access to any partner vendor endpoints if we need to run cross-vendor comparisons in parallel

Shared folder (read/write): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz-example

I'll run a short smoke test Mon 8/23 afternoon (PT) and share the test harness so you can inspect the requests. If anything changes on your side, ping me here.

Thanks - looking forward to results.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
